_doc: rubric.json — THE KEYSTONE of the Forest Builder kit-matcher. One shared vocabulary both the dossiers (arborist/dossiers/*.json) and the ingested parts (chassis/bark/leaf/overlay) speak. The matcher (Stage 1, §7), the readiness dashboard (§8), the reference-driven viewer (§9), and the ingest auto-tagger (§4) all derive from this. Get it right and they fall out of it; get it wrong and every layer inherits the confusion. Authored Stage 0 (2026-06-18) by agent Hortus against scratch/FOREST-BUILDER-KIT-MATCHER.md §2 + §7.2; SEEDED from the live library (species-map.json, leaf-pack-bindings.json, public/textures/leaves|bark, _chassis-curation.json), NOT greenfielded. Nothing renders from this file — it is data only.

discipline.atomic: Each axis is one indivisible characteristic.
discipline.orthogonal: Each axis is dial-able without disturbing the others (size independent of habit, age conducts several but is itself one dial).
discipline.complete: Every characteristic the rubric NAMES has a knob or a pick that generates it. Two characteristics are deliberately excluded (see nonAxes) so completeness stays honest.
discipline.plainLanguage: Operator-facing names are plain ('spreading', not 'deliquescent Troll's-model'). Scientific terms appear only as aliases for ingest-normalization.

axisSchema.name: operator-facing axis name
axisSchema.kind: enum | scalar | ordinal | dual | curve | band
axisSchema.values: enum/ordinal value-set (canonical tokens) — present iff discrete
axisSchema.home: where this lives in code today (the consolidation target)
axisSchema.tagging: auto | draft-then-ratify | human-only | operator — how a part gets this tag on ingest (§4)
axisSchema.orthogonality: the note proving this axis is independently dial-able
axisSchema.seededFrom: the live-library field/asset this axis's vocabulary was harvested from

axes.name: Habit / silhouette
axes.plain: The overall shape you'd read from across the street.
axes.home: chassis bbox aspect + branch-angle stats; today implicit in survey-deleaf morphology guess and _chassis meta.morphology ('broadleaf'/'conifer' only — too coarse, this axis refines it)
axes.orthogonality: Independent of size — a small and a large tree can both be 'spreading'.
axes.seededFrom: _chassis-curation.json displayNames (Weeping Willow→weeping, Red Maple/Maple→oval, European Linden→oval) + meta.morphology; species-map implicit habit
axes.note: Picking a different chassis-core IS the habit assignment; there is no per-part compatibility matrix (chassis is free geometry). Silhouette variety = pick a different core, NOT limb surgery (§2.1, locked).

axes.name: Size (height)
axes.plain: How big the tree actually is.
axes.home: tree-bounds.js → canopyByVariant (live, sole consumer bake-look.js:29); Brief-20 recenter sets Y-min 0 so height is the real metric extent
axes.orthogonality: Independent of habit and of leaf.size — the WHOLE-tree extent, not the leaf's.

axes.name: Lean
axes.plain: Is it leaning because the MODEL is crooked (fix it) or because this VARIETY leans (keep it)?
axes.home: correct → transform.rotation (Brief 19, baked once into geometry); morph → deformer center (Brief 3A uDeformLeanRange, per-instance continuum)
axes.orthogonality: The same visual degree of freedom carries TWO intents; the rubric keeps them distinct so a correction is never mistaken for an identity and vice-versa. Collapsing them is the bug this axis exists to prevent (§2.1).
axes.seededFrom: Birch + Redbud dossiers (both lean as a VARIETY trait — mode=morph; distinct from a crooked scan = mode=correct)

axes.name: Wood density
axes.plain: How much wood/branch texture fills the silhouette.
axes.orthogonality: Wood-fill of the silhouette, independent of leaf.occupancy (canopy fill) and of habit.
axes.seededFrom: not in current data — drafted; Birch/Bald Cypress = sparse(airy), maples = medium/dense

axes.name: Bark pattern
axes.plain: What the bark pattern reads as.
axes.home: species-map.barkMorph (surface the human NAME, never 'Bark003'); the 5 opaque public/textures/bark/Bark0NN dirs map INTO these types (draft) — Bark003/004/007/012/015 are ambientCG CC0 sources, the Library Builder (§4.5) renames them to type on disk
axes.orthogonality: The pattern class, independent of bark.color (hue/value) and the scalar bark detail knobs.

barkDirMap._note: DRAFT only — the 5 Bark0NN dirs are NOT deploy-ready ('the barks look bad', §0). Mapping seeded from species-map references; operator ratifies. Quality is Stage-2/3 work.

axes.name: Bark color
axes.orthogonality: Hue/value of the bark, independent of bark.type (pattern). A grey furrowed and a brown furrowed are the same type, different color.

axes.name: Furrow depth
axes.home: master bark shader knob (§6, barkDetail machinery — shipped)
axes.orthogonality: One detail knob of the furrowed/ridged types; independent of plate_size and scale_frequency.

axes.name: Plate size
axes.orthogonality: Detail knob of the plated type only.

axes.name: Scale frequency
axes.orthogonality: Detail knob of the scaly type only.

axes.name: Exfoliation / peel
axes.home: master bark shader knob — the mottled/exfoliating HARD CASE; needs a SECOND mask channel for spatial color variation (§6, Stage 3)
axes.orthogonality: Detail knob of exfoliating/mottled types; Birch (species #10) forces it.
axes.seededFrom: Birch dossier (salmon/cinnamon peeling) — the Stage-3 bark gap

axes.name: Leaf shape
axes.home: species-map.leafMorph + leaf-pack-bindings.morphology + pack meta.morphology (high-confidence, auto from pack meta)
axes.orthogonality: The single-leaf OUTLINE, independent of leaf.size (how big) and leaf.ways (how it attaches). A small and a large leaf can both be 'ovate'.
axes.FINDING_needle_scale: needle + scale were ADDED to this enum by Hortus (Stage 0). §2.3 of FOREST-BUILDER-KIT-MATCHER.md prints the value-set WITHOUT them, yet §12 forces Bald Cypress (#9, 'scale foliage') and the live roster carries Pine (needle). Omitting them breaks the rubric's COMPLETENESS promise. Botanically, Taxodium (bald cypress) is NEEDLE-like (linear, two-ranked sprays — confirmed by the reference research), NOT broad 'scale' like juniper/thuja; the brief's 'scale' label is loose. Both values are included; bald-cypress is tagged 'needle'. FLAGGED to Boz/Jacob for the vocabulary gate.

axes.name: Arrangement
axes.plain: How the leaf cards attach and orient on the twig.
axes.home: MISSING TODAY — new (§5). Rides the existing leaf-attachment anchor system (generate-salon.js#buildLeafGeometryFromAttachments + leafAttachmentTags); the May handoff named it 'cluster grammar' and never built it.
axes.orthogonality: How cards ATTACH/ORIENT, independent of silhouette (one leaf's shape) and color. Load-bearing for willow/locust/ginkgo/ash identity — without it all read as generic broadleaf scatter.
axes.seededFrom: phyllotaxy is exhaustively annotated botanically (a harvested list); not in any card geometry today

axes.name: Leaf size
axes.legibilityFloor: the card's real-metre extent must keep the leaf above ~1px at viewer distance; the operator multiplier (0.7–1.4×) cannot reach below it
axes.plain: How big the leaf reads — never bare.
axes.home: DERIVE at bake from canopyByVariant (live) + pack.meta.naturalSize (cm, PRESENT but UNUSED today). The carried-forward Espalier §3.1 fix, demoted from a patch to an axis.
axes.orthogonality: The LEAF's metric extent, independent of chassis.size (whole-tree extent). The bug today: BASE_CARD_SIZE (0.5m) × scale is unitless, so a leaf on a 30m Linden equals one on an 8m Magnolia and small leaves fall below a pixel → bare winter chassis.
axes.seededFrom: pack meta.naturalSize (palmate 10cm, lobed 12cm, heart 10cm, lanceolate 8cm, needle 15cm, ovate_large 15cm)

axes.name: Front / back two-tone

dual.back: second ramp off the same silhouette

axes.plain: Two-tone shimmer (silver maple, poplar) — the paler underside flashing in wind.
axes.home: orphaned tintFront / tintBack + doubleSided:true — WIRE them to this axis (§6)
axes.orthogonality: Two ramps off ONE silhouette; independent of the silhouette shape and of leaf.color's harmonization band (which applies to both ramps).
axes.seededFrom: Silver Maple dossier (STRONG silver underside — the defining trait) + Green Ash/Red Maple/Birch (mild)

axes.name: Color harmonization
axes.LOCKED: 2026-06-18 operator reframe — HARMONIZE value+saturation, PRESERVE hue per species.
axes.plain: Harmonized to one lit world — dead-dark lifted, fake-bright tamed; species KEEP their distinct hues.
axes.home: posterize substrate + ramp LUT (§6, the SHIPPED bark gradient-LUT machinery, 256×1, sha1-deduped, single Bloom-stable program); per-species hue from species-map.tints
axes.orthogonality: A value+saturation ENVELOPE, NOT a hue target. A maple-green and an oak-green stay distinct hues but read as belonging to one lit world — harmonized, not unified.
axes.seededFrom: species-map.tints.summer per species (maple #3a7b30, oak #3d6f30, ash drafted, etc. — each keeps its hue)
axes.supersedes: Espalier §3.2 'normalize to a green-band' (which would have collapsed hue) — REJECTED. The band is a value/saturation envelope, not a hue collapse.

axes.name: Seasonal ramp
axes.plain: Summer-green → gold → russet → bare across the year.
axes.home: year-long tree (ARCHITECTURE.md §Phase F Layer 2, annualCycle exists); the gradient ramp IS the color engine — summer/transitioning/dead as a day-of-year curve
axes.orthogonality: The TIME axis of color; orthogonal to leaf.color's harmonization band (which clamps every anchor's value/saturation).
axes.seededFrom: species-map.tints (buds/spring/summer/fall/winter) — the ramp seed, migrated verbatim per species
axes.cardinality: deciduous ≈ up to 6 anchors (incl. bare winter); evergreen ≈ 2 (no leaf-drop). Bald Cypress = deciduous CONIFER: needle sprays AND a bare-winter anchor.

axes.name: Canopy density
axes.orthogonality: Canopy FILL, independent of chassis.density (wood fill) and leaf.size. Owns leaf-shed; a true dead-leaf SHAPE change (curl) is a deferred edge, not v1.

axes.name: Overlay
axes.home: species-map.hasFlowers; Phase F Layer 3 per-Look packs (largely unbuilt). Rides the SAME card pipeline as leaves (public/textures/leaves/shapes/<pack>/) with resolution-order ABOVE the botanical default.
axes.orthogonality: A first-class part-type layered over leaves, not a leaf special-case. Crabapple/Redbud→flowers, Honey Locust→thorns, Sweetgum→fruit (gumballs), fall litter→seasonal-props.

axes.name: Maturity
axes.plain: One dial that ages the whole tree.
axes.home: composes deformer envelope + chassis.size + bark coarseness TOGETHER (brief §1.1)
axes.orthogonality: The one deliberate 'conductor' axis — orthogonal to every other (a young and a mature tree can share habit/silhouette/bark type) but DRIVES several at once, so the operator turns one dial, not three kept-in-sync.
axes.seededFrom: not in current data — drafted as the cross-cutting master dial

similarityMatrices._doc: §7.2 — the hand-authored near/far tables that ARE the matcher's taste (the single place human taste re-enters, §15.1). For each enum axis: value → { neighborValue: distance }. distance 0 = identity (implicit), 1 = near/adjacent (workable when an axis tol ≥ 1), 2 = stretch. Any pair NOT listed = 'far' (use farDistance). Symmetric by construction. STUBS — authored from botany + the seed library; the operator edits these as the library grows. The matcher reads: withinTol = distance ≤ required.tol; a HARD axis out of tol drops an option from 'workable' to 'stretch'.

leaf.silhouette._note: Mostly an IDENTITY axis (hard, tol 0) — a maple is not workable as an oak. Similarity exists only to rank STRETCH options when no exact silhouette is in hand.

scalarTolerance._doc: §7.2 — scalar axes (size, color-band) use percentage distance, not a matrix. distance = |actual − target| / target; withinTol = distance ≤ required.tol (e.g. tol 0.4 = ±40%). The legibility floor on leaf.size is a HARD clamp underneath — a too-small leaf is never workable regardless of tol.

ordinalTolerance._doc: §7.2 — ordinal axes (chassis.density) — adjacent buckets are workable. sparse↔medium = 1, medium↔dense = 1, sparse↔dense = 2.

nonAxes._doc: §2.6 — deliberately EXCLUDED so completeness stays honest. The rubric promises completeness OVER THE AXES IT DECLARES; these are explicitly outside that promise.
nonAxes.branch-angle / limb-count / scaffold-cou: Would require the limb graph we don't have (chassis arrive flat-merged, 1–3 WOOD prims). Silhouette variety = pick a different core, NOT limb surgery.
nonAxes.canopy-asymmetry / per-branch-jitter (3C: Needs inverse-transpose normals the per-instance deformer deliberately avoids. Deferred.
